sources.officialityEvidence: The current page is published by the South Sudan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation on mofaic.gov.ss. Its WordPress API record shows it was modified 5 December 2024 and supplies the Ministry’s country-by-country visa and fee table. The site certificate was expired during review, so normal TLS clients reject the page; this must be rechecked once the Ministry restores valid HTTPS.

policies.title: South Sudan: four MFA-listed visa-exempt nationalities
policies.summary: MFA’s current country-by-country visa-eligibility table marks Egypt, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda “EXEMPTED” with zero quoted entry-visa fees. It directly supports a nationality-wide visa exemption for the listed ordinary-passport short visitor cohort, rather than a visa on arrival or electronic authorization.
conditions: The published table does not state a duration, an effective date, passport-type qualifications, permitted purpose or entry-point limitations. This normalization is limited to its explicit country-level “EXEMPTED” rows and remains subject to ordinary border, health, security, admissibility and documentary checks.

MFA says bilateral relations can affect visa treatment. Its general page separately discusses visas on arrival, embassy processing, transit visas, and diplomatic, official and service passports; none is folded into this ordinary-passport visitor exemption.

The official eVisa portal provides a downloadable electronically issued visa for approved applicants. It is not an ETA, and this policy does not require it for the four explicitly exempt nationalities.

The Trade Information Hub’s statement that “most” travellers can obtain a visa on arrival has no nationality schedule. It does not establish an arrival-visa complement or alter the explicit MFA exemptions.

Work, residence, long stays, transit, invitation or entry-permit cases, foreign South Sudanese travelling on foreign passports, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien and other special documents are outside this policy.
